operator_io_quirks: All identifiers are simple ASCII CamelCase with underscores; no spaces, no quoting hazards beyond the standard double-quote rule.
Tiny DB: every table <=15 rows; read_schema's 300k cap never triggers, original_values are complete.

Assets_in_Events declares the SAME FK (Event_ID -> Events.Event_ID) twice in the DDL; pragma foreign_key_list returns two rows for one (child_t,child_c) key -> the fks dict collapses them, harmless but must not assert uniqueness.
Assets_in_Events has no FK on Asset_ID (only Event_ID); Asset_ID is a composite-PK member with no parent -> TS Number sampler, no consistency.
Parties_in_Events PK is composite (Party_ID, Event_ID); both members are also FKs -> composite-PK member max_l0=30 path applies to both.
Events.Address_ID is nullable FK to Addresses; original has 0 nulls but 8 distinct of 15 -> TS may emit NULLs (parent empty case) and duplicates.
Events.Channel_ID is NOT NULL but has NO declared FK (dangling reference to Channels by name only) -> TS treats it as a plain Number column, no consistency with Channels.
Products.Product_Price is DECIMAL(20,4) stored as real; TS Number scale=20 precision=4 -> range [-1e20,1e20], wildly wider than observed 932..3298.

CHAR(15) columns (Product_Type_Code, Event_Type_Code, Role_Code) dispatch to String(length=15); observed values are short enums ('Books','Food','Organizer','Participant','Trade Show') -> TS will emit random 0..15-char strings, not enum members.
VARCHAR(255) columns dispatch to String(length=255) -> TS fresh strings up to 255 chars, far longer than observed ('Mutual','Good','Bad','145').

Channels.Other_Details holds numeric-looking text ('145','348','933') in a VARCHAR column -> String sampler will add str(i+1)/str(i-1) neighbours and contaminate; storage class text, declared VARCHAR, consistent.
Addresses.address_details contains embedded newlines and commas; String sampler's CHARSET has no newline/comma -> fresh values never reproduce that shape.
operator_ts_expectations: Every PK is INTEGER -> Number fuzzer, scale=0, int perturbation (+-1,+-2); PK uniqueness enforced by sample_fresh_primary_keys, so PKs stay distinct but drift far outside 1..15.

FK columns (Events.Address_ID/Finance_ID/Location_ID, Products_in_Events.*, Parties_in_Events.*, Agreements.Event_ID, Assets_in_Events.Event_ID) draw from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> duplicates and NULLs (Address_ID) appear; referential integrity holds only because parent values are reused.
Events.Channel_ID and Assets_in_Events.Asset_ID are NOT FK-consistent -> random Numbers, so joins Events-Channels and Assets_in_Events-Assets will often be empty or partial in generated units.

String columns get 5 original samples + distinct literal-pool values, then p=0.2 fresh random strings with 0.5 contaminate -> enum columns (Product_Type_Code, Event_Type_Code, Role_Code) lose their small domain; equality/IN predicates on those codes will mostly miss.
Product_Price Number(scale=20) draws uniform in +-1e20 -> price comparisons (>, <, BETWEEN) almost never match the observed 900..3300 band; likely FN driver for price filters.
Finances.Other_Details has only 3 distinct ('Mutual','Good','Bad') but String sampler will emit long random strings -> predicates like ='Good' or IN(...) rarely hit.

Channels.Other_Details numeric-text: String sampler adds str(i+1)/str(i-1) for int-like elements, so some numeric neighbours survive, but fresh draws are alphabetic -> numeric comparisons on this column are unreliable.

Composite PKs (Parties_in_Events, Assets_in_Events) get max_l0=30 -> fresh draws capped, more element reuse, so duplicate (Party_ID,Event_ID) pairs are dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys; ties in GROUP BY on these pairs are plausible.

Small tables (Assets=3, Parties=7) with level-based sizing (level0=1+30u, x4 per level) -> generated sizes can be much larger than original, changing cardinality ratios; COUNT(*) comparisons against original are meaningless.

No CHECK constraints, no NOT NULL on most non-PK columns -> TS's non-enforcement of NOT NULL/CHECK is invisible here except Events.Channel_ID/Finance_ID/Location_ID NOT NULL (TS Number never emits NULL, so fine).
No text-stored dates, no booleans, no time columns -> Date/Time/Bool fuzzers never fire; all misses come from Number range and String domain loss.
